evidence: Jan 2026 State of the Commonwealth/budget proposes $159M for mandatory educator raises and higher per-pupil K-12 funding.
Jan 2026 State of the Commonwealth/budget proposes a $125 million rural hospital fund.
Jan 2026 budget proposes $150 million for the Affordable Housing Trust Fund, which he says would leverage about $1B in new housing.
Jan 2026 State of the Commonwealth calls for hiring more law enforcement and paying them better, plus a reentry campus; no new dollar figure.
Jan 2026 budget proposes $100 million to lower the cost of kynect coverage and fully funds Medicaid; related subsidy, not a public option.
Jan 2026 budget proposes $50M for career and technical education facilities and a prison reentry campus with KCTCS vocational training; no apprenticeship plan.
Signed HB 95 capping insulin copays at $30 for a 30-day supply (Mar 2021).
Vetoed HB 312 (concealed carry at 18-20) and HB 78 (gun-seller liability shield) in Apr 2026; both overridden. Backed a red-flag-style law in 2023.
Proposed $141M over two years to keep higher child care subsidy rates and expand assistance for children 3 and under (Dec 2023); 2026 budget adds Pre-K for All.
Touted 988 growth and $40M+ in school mental health grants; signed 2026 HB 169 and HB 178 expanding mental health coverage (May 2026).
Vetoed SB 349, which made it harder to retire fossil plants, citing his all-of-the-above energy policy (Apr 2024); no clean-power standard proposed.
Signed SB 4 (2025), setting state AI governance rules, disclosure of AI use, and remedies for deepfake election ads (Mar 2025); not kids-specific.
Jan 2025 executive budget proposed nearly $105M for housing supply and affordability, including a $50M public-private housing program.
Jan 2025 budget proposed $19.2M for behavioral health, including $7.8M for youth crisis care and $2M for rural crisis supports, plus a new State Hospital.
Jan 2025 budget proposed $60M for 2% annual increases in the K-12 funding formula; a modest raise, alongside a $44.3M ESA proposal.
Signed HB 1160 banning personal devices during K-12 instruction, in effect Aug 2025; a related kids-tech step, not an AI or online-safety law.
Backed Trump's 145% China tariffs while conceding retaliation will hurt ND farmers (Apr 2025); later said Canada tariffs strained ties (Feb 2026).
Signed the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge that data centers pay full cost of new power and grid upgrades (Jul 2026); voluntary, no state law.
Signed a 2025 law giving employers a 50% tax credit for child care stipends to workers (May 2025); narrower than expanded public subsidies.
Signed HB 1588 loosening concealed-carry rules, incl. dropping the duty to inform police and allowing guns on campuses (Apr 23 2025).
Governor-elect plans to simplify housing permitting and regulation and build workforce housing on unused government land via public-private deals (Nov 2026).
Governor-elect says her transition will focus on workforce development and job retraining with local mayors; no specific program yet (Nov 2026).
Governor-elect cited her work on the federal employer child care tax credit and wants more care options for parents; no state plan (Nov 2026).
Touts the $1B Rural Health Transformation Fund she worked on (Oct 2026) but voted for the OBBBA Medicaid cuts that created it (Jul 2025).
Lead sponsor of the Kids Online Safety Act, S.1748, reintroduced in 2025; pressed Congress to pass it (Dec 2025). Federal bill, not a state plan.
As senator voted against the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (Jun 2022), which funded red-flag programs; federal vote, no state gun plan stated.
Backed Trump's tariffs: 'President Trump is right' on his approach, calling the old tariff structure unfair to workers (Apr 2025).
Jan 2026 State of the State proposes a Workforce Readiness & Opportunity Act to expand micro-credentials and portable benefits, plus more workforce-training money.
Jan 2026 State of the State urged lawmakers to quickly authorize the $199M federal Rural Health Transformation plan; no new state money or Medicaid-rate plan.
Signed HB 2003 restricting student smartphone use during class (Apr 2025); a related kids-tech step, not an AI or online-safety law.
Signed HB 2014 barring local limits on data centers (May 2025), but signed the White House pledge that data centers pay full power and grid costs (Jul 2026).
Signed 287(g) agreements with ICE for the National Guard, State Police and Corrections: 'proud to partner with ICE' (Aug 2025).
Signed HB 4106 extending permitless carry to 18- to 20-year-olds (Apr 1 2026).
Seeks $1.44B to keep six coal plants running 20 more years under a coal/gas/nuclear-led energy plan (Nov 2025); no statement on clean mandates found.
FY2027 budget he signed gives teachers and other state workers a 3% raise (Mar 2026); no formula overhaul, and $276M goes to HOPE private-school accounts.
Campaign pledged to strengthen rural hospitals and EMS and said yes to championing a state-funded perpetuity fund to sustain rural health gains (Jul 2026).
Campaign lists expanding behavioral health capacity as a goal of his healthcare strike team; no funding plan given (Jul 2026).
Questionnaire prioritizes strong career and technical education and apprenticeships, with employers, schools and colleges coordinating (Jun 2026).
Campaign pledges to strengthen public safety and back officers and first responders with training and resources; no specific funding plan (2026).
Campaign says he supported 'stronger concealed carry laws' (expanding carry) and sponsored a bill restoring gun rights to hundreds (2026).
Said the legislature 'finally made progress' on the school funding model but more work remains (Apr 2026); no funding pledge.
